transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have a medically stable patient being evaluated for transfer to our hospital-at-home program tomorrow. As we do every day, I need each of you to give your verbal report on the patient's readiness and care requirements in your area before I can finalize the acceptance decision and care plan. Let's go in our standard round-robin order: attending physician, then physical therapist, then social worker, then utilization-review coordinator. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good morning, Marisol. I'll start us off. From the medical standpoint, the patient is medically stable and appropriate for transfer to the hospital-at-home program. I've signed an order for ceftriaxone 2 grams by IV at 10:00 each day for three days, and this treatment can be administered through the hospital-at-home nursing visits rather than requiring the patient to remain inpatient. I believe the patient is ready for transfer from a medical perspective.

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Chen. I'll go next with the physical therapy report. I conducted a home-entry assessment and found twelve stairs at the front entrance. The patient can manage them with supervision, but per program policy, a stair-assist rail needs to be installed before arrival. The good news is the equipment vendor has confirmed installation will be completed by 07:00 tomorrow, so that requirement will be met prior to transfer. From a mobility standpoint, the patient is appropriate for the program with supervision for stairs once the rail is in place.

transcript.text: Thank you, Nia. I'll give the social work report now. From a social support standpoint, I've assessed the patient's home care resources. The patient's spouse is available to provide in-home support from 08:00 through 20:00, and a named neighbor has agreed to serve as the overnight escalation contact from 20:00 through 08:00. This means the patient will have continuous coverage and a clear escalation pathway around the clock. From a social work perspective, the patient's home support system is appropriate for the hospital-at-home program.

transcript.text: Thank you, Owen. I'll give the utilization-review report now. From a utilization-review standpoint, I've confirmed that the payer has approved hospital-at-home coverage for this patient. The approval covers exactly 72 hours of care, with two covered in-person nursing visits per day, scheduled at 08:00 and 20:00. This coverage window and visit schedule will need to be factored into the care plan, particularly in coordinating with the nursing team to ensure the ceftriaxone IV administration at 10:00 aligns with the approved visit times. From a utilization-review perspective, the patient is appropriate for the program within these approved coverage parameters.
